newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Kyrgyzstan capital cut off from Uzbek gas supply.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyzstan capital cut off from Uzbek gas supply.

text.p: Supplies of Uzbek natural gas to the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek -- reduced recently due to Kyrgyzstan's debts -- came to a complete halt on Tuesday, an official from the former Soviet republic's gas company said.
Residents of the city of 700,000 people were warned not to use gas stoves or other gas appliances to avoid leaks and explosions.

"Due to an unseasonally cold snap over the last few days, the pressure in gas pipelines, which was low anyway, has fallen even further," Nurzhakyp Suimaliyev, deputy director general of the state Kyrgyzgazmunaizat company, told Reuters.
He said pressure fell in April when Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan's only natural gas supplier, cut deliveries to the mountainous republic because of the debts.

In line with an agreement between the governments of the two Central Asian states, Uzbekistan is to supply Kyrgyzstan with 1.15 billion cubic metres of gas this year. Officials could not be reached immediately to say how much Kyrgyzstan pays for gas.
